analyst.summary: Piramal Pharma posted a genuine FY26 consolidated net loss (Rs 325.94cr on Rs 8,869cr revenue, ~10.4% full-year EBITDA margin) that the quant model correctly flags via negative ROE/PE, but our own PIT reconciliation shows three consecutive quarters of sequential EBITDA-margin recovery (5.5% -> 7.8% -> 9.2% -> 16.7%) into Q4FY26, tracking a real external tailwind -- US biopharma/biotech funding up 75% YoY in H2FY26 -- feeding the CDMO segment's (~60% of sales) RFP pipeline after a de-stocking-driven trough. Complex Hospital Generics (inhalation-anesthesia, 47% US share) and India Consumer Healthcare (Power Brands +24%, e-commerce +48%) are steadier, moat-backed contributors. Net debt has not increased despite US$94mn of FY26 capex and a bolt-on acquisition, and the promoter group has pledged zero shares through the loss year. USFDA risk is real but not yet acute -- three sites drew Form-483s in ~14 months, but none has reached OAI/warning-letter status. Against a thin 2.7x interest cover and an aggressive FY30 aspiration ($2bn revenue / 25% EBITDA margin, implying ~17-18% revenue CAGR plus ~1,400bps of margin expansion that the company has already partly missed once), this is a genuine, evidence-based recovery story rather than a broken one -- but not yet proven enough to call a confident Hold. Call: Hold, escalated.
